title: Report Contiguous Dates
prompt: Report continuous intervals of the same period_state between 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-31. Return period_state, start_date, and end_date.
expected_query: WITH timeline AS (SELECT 'failed' AS period_state, fail_date AS status_date FROM failed WHERE CAST(fail_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-01-31' UNION ALL SELECT 'succeeded' AS period_state, success_date AS status_date FROM succeeded WHERE CAST(success_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-01-31'), numbered AS (SELECT period_state, status_date, CAST(status_date AS DATE) - CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY period_state ORDER BY status_date) AS INTEGER) AS group_key FROM timeline) SELECT period_state, MIN(status_date) AS start_date, MAX(status_date) AS end_date FROM numbered GROUP BY period_state, group_key;
explanation: Combine both status tables, assign row numbers per status, then group continuous dates using date - row_number.
hints: Normalize both tables into one timeline.
Use MIN and MAX for each interval.
common_mistakes: Grouping failed and succeeded rows together.
Using one row_number across all statuses instead of partitioning by status.
